heroTitle: Hair Fall: Shedding, Thinning And What Can Be Done
shortDesc: How to tell normal shedding from real hair loss, what causes it, and the treatments that slow it down and rebuild density.
intro: Everyone sheds 50 to 100 hairs a day. Hair fall becomes a concern when the shedding increases, the parting widens, the hairline recedes or the scalp starts to show. Finding the cause is the first step, because pattern hair loss, stress-related shedding, nutritional deficiency and scalp disease all look similar in the shower drain but need different treatment.

At Skin Essence in Kalyani Nagar, hair and scalp problems are one of Dr. Daksha Patel's special interests. Every hair consultation includes trichoscopy, a magnified examination of the scalp and hair roots that distinguishes thinning from shedding, and blood tests when the history points to a deficiency or a hormonal cause. Only then are medicines or procedures suggested.
causes: Androgenetic (pattern) hair loss in men and women, driven by genetics and hormones
Telogen effluvium: sudden shedding after illness, fever, childbirth, surgery or severe stress
Iron, vitamin D, vitamin B12 or protein deficiency
Dandruff, seborrhoeic dermatitis and other scalp conditions
Tight hairstyles, heat styling, chemical treatments and hard water

howWeTreat.title: Diagnose with trichoscopy
howWeTreat.description: The scalp and roots are examined under magnification to see whether follicles are miniaturising, shedding or inflamed, and the pattern is photographed.

howWeTreat.title: Test and correct
howWeTreat.description: Blood tests for iron stores, vitamin D, B12, thyroid and, in women, hormones identify causes that can be corrected.

howWeTreat.title: Medical treatment
howWeTreat.description: Topical or low-dose oral minoxidil, anti-androgens where appropriate, and treatment of dandruff or scalp inflammation form the base of the plan.

howWeTreat.title: Regrowth boosters
howWeTreat.description: GFC, PRP, exosomes, hair fillers or hair threads are added where extra density is wanted, with progress reviewed by photographs every three months.

selfCare: Eat enough protein and iron; crash diets are a common trigger for shedding.
Wash the scalp two to three times a week; a clean scalp grows better hair than an oiled one.
Avoid tight ponytails, heat styling and chemical straightening while hair recovers.
Do not self-prescribe supplements; correct only what a test shows is low.
whenToSeeDoctor: You are losing clearly more hair than usual for over six weeks.
The parting is widening or the hairline is receding.
There are bald patches, or itching, scaling or pain on the scalp.
Hair fall follows childbirth, illness or a new medicine and is not settling.

faqs.a: Shedding from stress, illness or deficiency usually stops once the trigger is corrected, and hair regrows over months. Pattern hair loss can be slowed and partly reversed with medicines and growth-factor treatments, but needs ongoing treatment to hold the result.

faqs.q: How much hair fall is normal?
faqs.a: Up to about 100 hairs a day is normal, more on wash days. What matters is a change: more hair on the pillow and in the drain than you are used to, or visible thinning.

faqs.q: Do hair oils and special shampoos help?
faqs.a: Oils condition the hair shaft but do not treat the cause of hair fall, and heavy oiling can worsen dandruff. Medicated shampoos help scalp conditions. Regrowth needs treatment of the actual cause.

faqs.q: How long before I see results?
faqs.a: Shedding usually reduces within 6 to 12 weeks of starting treatment, and new growth shows at 4 to 6 months, which is why we review with photographs rather than day-to-day impressions.
